scope: Native task controls in the Mac host menu and popover handback to an unchanged native document
productionChanges: Expose the existing task-scoped local control snapshot as a published property and reuse its existing validated handler from the host menu.
Show Take control or Let AI continue, plus Stop AI, for retained native and browser tasks.
Dismiss the host popover synchronously before its Resume handler returns control to the executor. Preserve native target validation.
findings: Source and Computer Use inspection confirmed the old host menu had no task controls. The first fixture could not compile, then its in-process AX walker returned no buttons; neither attempt is counted as a valid UI regression.

The third initial run used Computer Use to inspect the rendered menu; its task-control button was absent. The fake executor also reported setup-needed because it claimed to need a helper. That fixture was corrected to declare its native capability without changing other test defaults.
Computer Use then operated all three rendered production buttons; independent executor cancellation and task-ledger assertions passed.
The first real popover handoff failed after Resume with zero confirmed mutations. The executor could not retain a focused native target while the popover remained open.
The corrected real run measured the native snapshot as unreadable while the popover was open, kept TextEdit as the frontmost app, and completed after the popover dismissed before Resume.

The successful real run has three approval presentations (one invalidated by takeover), two approved/confirmed MCP effects, exact expected Unicode editor/file contents, and the document window retained until fixture cleanup.
Fourteen focused local/native/browser/ledger/revocation/held-input regressions pass with zero warnings or skips. The real native run retains the existing main-thread UI-unresponsiveness warning.
computerUseObservations: host-native-menu-red-03: rendered Start Listening and status, but no task controls.
host-native-menu-green-01: Take control changed Working to Paused; Let AI continue changed Paused to Working; Stop ended the fixture after the independent stop assertions.

host-native-menu-textedit-01 and -02: actual NSPopover showed AI Approval Required, then visibly Paused after Take control. Resume closed the task UI during the post-click observation; authoritative task reports distinguish failure from success.
host-native-menu-final-01: screenshot inspected for readable, unclipped button layout. Computer Use repeated Take control, Resume and Stop on the final build; independent tests passed.
Post-click App quit/timeoutReached results are retained as observation limits; completion claims rely on terminal xcodebuild/xcresult and independent native/ledger evidence.
limitations: Production MenuContent renders in an owned test panel. The real task uses NSPopover with the same transient/content/makeKey configuration as AppDelegate, anchored to an owned test panel rather than the installed status item.
The installed app was not replaced or restarted. AppDelegate callback wiring compiled; the normal installed status-item launch itself was not exercised.
Task storage and transport are isolated. No physical phone, provider login or full CloudKit enrollment was tested.
The native task is a previously qualified document goal, now testing rendered local handoff. This is not new language or cross-app generalization evidence.
The bundled worker was absent in 252 samples in the passing native run. Apple semantic planning still ran; whole-app 12 GB/heat qualification remains open.
Remaining shared UI responsiveness warning is not fixed. Browser sign-in popup interactions through the newly exposed host controls still need explicit qualification.

Original host PID 67555, main commit 603e79e9f877a4a1c9a0b462d8db4da06dc46cf2 and stash f11908b0e0617388bec0a3d4a9542c9c5694f174 were preserved. Final process inventory found no test host, TextEdit, MacControlMCP or llama-server processes.
